text: On the bus back to Seoul, Taeo couldn't shake it. The man who always said everything was fine had told him never to enter a gate.
Nib asked what Grandpa had said at the bus door. Nothing, Taeo said. Nib had heard it himself, but let it go.
Twenty days to the review. Nib kept scouting at Minho's yard, flagging hazards like a bent screen foot. Taeo got very good at watching.
The receipts piled up in their folder. Nib kept his pay in a biscuit tin.
Eunchae taught him Hangul in the break room. He proudly sounded out his first long word: cross-contamination. From her food licence flashcards.
The construct took Taeo's night shifts. Watching it stand motionless after work, Nib asked who took over from it. Nobody. Constructs didn't tire. Nobody came for it, Nib observed.
The night before the review, Taeo wrote out everything he would say for Nib. Nib pointed out that the panel would be asking him.
The next morning, they reached the agency. Eunchae's message: stop apologising, and Nib, don't rush your vowels.
Security kept Nib's knife until they left. Don't drop it, he warned the guard. It was a good knife.
Upstairs, Pyo was handing coffee to Chae's supervisor like an old friend.
The supervisor quietly urged Chae to withdraw her arrival report. She refused. Nib wasn't theirs, and her name was already on it.
In the hearing room, Nib counted one door. The chair opened the hearing. Kanghan wanted Nib reclassified as a construct. She called him 'it.'
Pyo argued that advanced constructs could imitate speech, learning which words moved people without understanding any of them. Nib reached for his knife and found an empty sheath.
Chae cited the arrival category in the 1995 Act, unused for twenty years. Shown a form with only hunter or construct, Nib had told her he wasn't a box.
Minho brought receipts for nine jobs, paid to Nib directly. And Nib had turned down a tenth job for a Hangul lesson. Minho had watched him choose.
Bae rushed in late, leaving his golem outside. He paid 640,000 won a month for a construct. He knew what one was. Nib wasn't one.
The chair asked Taeo what Nib was. Taeo folded away his notes. 'You should ask Nib.'
Nib stepped out from behind the lectern, chose a spot facing the door, and admitted he was afraid of rooms with one exit. The chair stopped writing. What was he?
A scout, Nib said. He kept watch at a wall above the lower path. Kett had been coming to take over.
Now Kett would find the post empty and come looking for him. Nib's fist trembled, but he kept his eyes on the panel.
'I'm someone's relief.'
Under the table, amber pulsed in Taeo's palm. Nib was letting him feel the trembling. The room went still. Bae ignored the red warning on his wrist and stayed.
Pyo took off his glasses. Mimicry could be very sophisticated, he said. Nib raised his open hand so everyone could see it shaking.
'Then why would I lie about being afraid?' For a moment, something like doubt crossed Pyo's face.
After the recess, the panel denied Kanghan's petition. Nib was a registered arrival. A person. Pending for twelve months, renewable.
Taeo laughed and cried at once. Nib handed him a napkin. 'You're leaking.' Chae closed her eyes and let out a long breath.
At registration, the clerk asked Nib to smile. He refused. The camera caught the scowl while Taeo tried not to laugh.
His new card said registered arrival, person, with Yoon Taeo as his linked partner. Nib read it slowly. He could read now. Slowly.
Knife back on his hip, Nib relaxed. Taeo handed Pyo back his business card.
Pyo pocketed it, unbothered. 'Pending isn't permanent, Mr. Yoon.'
On the steps, Chae caught them with a list of gates still open. One Grade E gate in a subway maintenance tunnel had only an entrance photo so far.
She had printed it because Nib liked paper. He held it next to his drawing of the watch post. The white stone inside the gate looked like the white patch beside his wall.
The gate was still open, for now. Nib looked up at Taeo. He wanted to go in.
Grandpa's warning came back. Taeo told him he couldn't go in.
Nib held up his new ID, steady. 'I didn't ask you to.'
